claims.label: Hill climb remains the practical default for validated internal onemax sizes.
validated_ranges: CI gate uses the representative large ablation row at length 128
claims.pass_condition: Representative internal ablation keeps hill_climb ahead of pure_ga on evaluations-to-target.
claims.warning_threshold: If the mean advantage stays positive but the CI overlaps zero or significance weakens, mark WARN.
claims.notes: This is an internal official claim only. Broad bitstring generalization is handled separately by family-conditioned external claims.

claims.label: Hill climb remains the family-conditional practical default on the tested monotone bitstring subset (OneMax, LeadingOnes).
claims.pass_condition: OneMax representative row keeps hill_climb ahead on evaluations-to-target and LeadingOnes keeps hill_climb ahead on final best fitness.
claims.warning_threshold: If only one monotone family row remains positive or significance weakens, mark WARN instead of PASS.
claims.notes: This is intentionally narrower than 'all bitstring problems'. Deceptive and multimodal families are tracked separately.

claims.label: A representative pure GA path may outperform hill climb on the tested deceptive trap subset.
claims.pass_condition: Trap representative row keeps official pure GA ahead of hill_climb and mutation_only_ea on final best fitness.
claims.warning_threshold: If only one comparator remains positive or the CI overlaps zero, mark WARN.
claims.notes: The wording stays narrow on purpose: a tested deceptive family may favor pure GA, not all deceptive problems.

claims.label: The tested Jump_k row is still too narrow to support a stable solver default.
claims.pass_condition: Jump_k representative row remains inconclusive rather than flipping into a stable default recommendation.
claims.warning_threshold: If one solver starts showing a stable positive CI, review the docs and possibly promote or demote the rule.
claims.notes: Report-only. It is more important to avoid overclaiming than to force a stable Jump_k default from one representative row.

claims.label: Greedy local search remains the family-conditional practical default on the tested uncorrelated knapsack subset.
claims.pass_condition: Uncorrelated family representative row keeps greedy_local_search ahead of the official pure GA path on feasible quality.
claims.warning_threshold: If greedy keeps a positive mean but loses significance or the CI overlaps zero, mark WARN.
claims.notes: This claim is intentionally limited to the tested uncorrelated family slice, not all knapsack instances.

claims.label: Seed-repair hybrid remains a family-conditional worth-trying path on the tested correlated knapsack subsets.
validated_ranges: kplib weakly correlated n=50 representative instance
kplib strongly correlated n=100 representative instance
claims.pass_condition: Weakly and strongly correlated representative rows keep seed_repair_hybrid ahead of greedy_local_search on feasible quality under matched evaluation budgets.
claims.warning_threshold: If only one correlated family remains positive or the CI overlaps zero, mark WARN.
claims.notes: This is not a broad external-wide knapsack default. It is a family-conditioned 'worth trying' rule with explicit runtime cost.

claims.label: The tested subset-sum-like knapsack slice remains experimental.
claims.pass_condition: Subset-sum representative row may stay positive, but it remains report-only until more structured families agree.
claims.warning_threshold: If the row turns negative or disappears, keep it experimental but note the drift.
claims.notes: The evidence is intentionally treated as exploratory so docs do not overstate structured-family support.

claims.label: Nearest-neighbor + 2-opt remains the externally supported practical default on the tested TSPLIB subset.
claims.pass_condition: Nearest-neighbor + 2-opt keeps lower route distance than the official pure GA path on both representative TSPLIB instances.
claims.warning_threshold: If only one representative TSPLIB instance remains positive or significance weakens, mark WARN.
claims.notes: This is the external practical default. The medium hybrid path remains internal-only and is tracked separately.

claims.label: The validated internal medium TSP hybrid remains a narrow quality-first path.
validated_ranges: internal medium size 20 representative ablation rows
claims.pass_condition: Official internal hybrid stays ahead of pure GA and retains a statistically supported distance edge over the cheap baseline at size 20.
claims.warning_threshold: If it still beats pure GA but loses the baseline edge, mark WARN and keep the path internal-only.
claims.notes: This path is deliberately narrow. Even when it passes internally, it is not promoted to an external practical default.

claims.label: Pure NSGA-II remains the externally supported default path over random archive on the tested ZDT subset.
claims.pass_condition: NSGA-II keeps higher hypervolume than random_archive on the tested ZDT2 and ZDT3 rows.
claims.warning_threshold: If only one tested ZDT family row remains positive or the CI overlaps zero, mark WARN.
claims.notes: The external claim is deliberately tied to the tested ZDT subset and to hypervolume-over-random support rather than a single scalar winner across all metrics.

claims.label: Large ZDT1 still requires a metric-priority tradeoff note rather than a one-best claim.
claims.pass_condition: Large ZDT remains documented as a metric-priority tradeoff instead of a one-size-fits-all winner.
claims.warning_threshold: If docs start phrasing large ZDT as a scalar one-best preset, review manually.
claims.notes: Report-only note claim. Governance here is primarily about preventing claim creep in docs.
